title: Acceptance evaluation refuses long-history items on a busy project: notes continuation requires a frozen global project_position, but Engram returns a fresh read cut per page
outcome: Acceptance evaluation refuses long-history items on a busy project: notes continuation requires a frozen global project_position, but Engram returns a fresh read cut per page
acceptance: acceptance_compact_notes_carrier (src/acceptance_evidence_selection.rs) no longer requires read_cut.project_position to be equal across notes+gates continuation pages, which matches Engram's work_record_window contract: a fresh read cut per call, with the selected index total and the immutable boundary validated. It still refuses a change of canonical work identity, of task or evidence basis, of notes_window.total, a newer offset that is not previous newer+shown, an empty page, and a repeated cursor.

A test drives a multi-page canonical discovery in which a write elsewhere in the project advances project_position between pages. The evaluation request is accepted, and the brief contains the paged evidence. A test where total changes between pages is still refused with the existing 409.

A test shows how a long note history (hundreds of notes, small pages) is handled within the discovery budget: either it pages within the time budget, or it stops paging with a recorded paging_stop and still evaluates. It must not fail with a 502 or a 409.

completion.summary:
acceptance_compact_notes_carrier no longer requires an equal read_cut.project_position across notes+gates pages; the identity, basis, total, offset, empty-page and cursor guards are kept. Optional notes paging now stops before each page with "time_budget" unless that page and every mandatory read after it still fit before discovery_deadline. The mandatory reads are held, full, the distinct selected records plus revalidation, and every binding page: div_ceil(listed + acceptance_omitted, 8), clamped to 1..=16, with all 16 reserved when the list is absent. A page that actually fails stays fatal.
